title: Energy cost of electron--positron conversion
html:
Remark. Energy cost of electron--positron conversion

The energy cost of converting an electron into a positron depends on what "convert" means. The QOU framework distinguishes three energy scales.

Standard physics: conversion is forbidden; only pair creation is possible. An isolated electron cannot become a positron — lepton number conservation forbids it. The minimum process is pair production: a photon near a nucleus creates an e^- e^+ pair, requiring

  E_{\gamma}  \geq  2m_ec^2 =  1.022  \text{MeV}.

The original electron is unchanged; a new pair appears from the photon's energy.

In the QOU: crossing energy of the trefoil. The electron is the left trefoil T_{2,3} with n_c = 3 positive crossings. Its crossing energy is

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(e^-)
  =  3q
   \approx  3  q_0
  =  3.330
  \quad (\text{in Skein units}).

The positron is the mirror T_{2,3}^{\sigma} with 3 negative crossings:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(e^+)
  =  -3q^{-1}
   \approx  -3 \times 0.9009
  =  -2.703
  \quad (\text{in Skein units}).

The crossing energy gap between the two chiralities is

  \Delta \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}
  =  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(e^-) - \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(e^+)
  =  3(q + q^{-1})
   \approx  6.033
  \quad (\text{in Skein units}).

This decomposes into symmetric and antisymmetric parts:

  3(q + q^{-1})
  = 
  \underbrace{3 \cdot 2 \cosh(\ln q)}_{\text{strong baseline}}
  = 
  6 \cosh(\ln q)
   \approx  6.033.

Three energy scales for "conversion".

Process Energy QOU description
Pair production (\gamma \to e^- e^+) 2m_e c^2 \approx 1.022 MeV New pair from photon; trefoil + mirror created at exceptional divisor
Crossing energy gap (one trefoil) 3(q + q^{-1}) \approx 6.03 Skein units Full reversal of all 3 crossings; maps to \Delta E = 6\cosh(\ln q)
Complex-q barrier (\theta = 0 \to \pi) Topological, not energetic Continuous rotation in pre-observable sector; no energy cost in observable sector

Physical interpretation of each route.

  1. Pair production at the exceptional divisor. When a photon with E \geq 2m_e encounters the blow-up locus, it can resolve into a trefoil--mirror pair. The energy 2m_e is not the crossing energy gap — it is the mass-energy of the two particles created. The crossing energies of e^- and e^+ have opposite sign and partially cancel in the pair:

      \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(e^-) + \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(e^+)
  =  3q - 3q^{-1}
  =  3(q - q^{-1})
   \approx  0.630
  \quad (\text{Skein units}).

    The residual 3(q - q^{-1}) > 0 is the net Coulomb repulsion of the pair — the antisymmetric part of the crossing energy that drives the e^- and e^+ apart after creation. The ratio

      \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  =  \tanh(\ln q)
   \approx  0.104

    measures the electromagnetic-to-strong ratio for the electron, consistent with \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} \sim 1/137 at low energies (the Skein ratio is at the constituent scale, not the running coupling scale).

  2. Direct chirality reversal (forbidden in observable sector). Flipping all 3 crossings of T_{2,3} to produce T_{2,3}^{\sigma} while keeping the same knot would require a topological transition through the unknot, but the trefoil is topologically stable. In the observable sector (q real, \theta = 0), no finite energy can accomplish this: the trefoil and its mirror are in different connected components of knot space.

  3. Complex-q rotation (pre-observable). In the complex substrate framework, the chirality operator \mathcal{X}_\varphi \colon \theta \to \theta + \varphi rotates continuously from electron to positron. This has zero energy cost in the pre-observable sector (the rotation is along a flat direction of the categorical action). The energy cost appears only upon projection to the observable sector, where the continuous rotation collapses to the discrete pair-creation event with threshold 2m_e.

Summary. The energy to "convert" an electron to a positron is either:

  • \infty (impossible within the observable sector — topologically forbidden),
  • 2m_e \approx 1.022 MeV (create a new pair at the exceptional divisor), or
  • 0 (in the pre-observable complex-q sector, chirality rotation is free but inaccessible to measurement).

The crossing energy gap 3(q + q^{-1}) in Skein units sets the algebraic distance between the two chiralities. Its physical manifestation is not a single energy threshold but the decomposition into symmetric binding (\cosh) and antisymmetric Coulomb (\sinh) channels.
